text:
Carolina comes in off a 4-1 loss at Nashville that ended a four-game winning streak, though the Hurricanes are still 4-1-0 in their last five and playing without Jordan Staal (calf). Jackson Blake has taken his spot on the second line. The Islanders have waited five days since a 4-0 loss to Edmonton, and they're missing Matias Maccelli, Calum Ritchie and Ryan Pulock. Simon Holmstrom has stepped into Maccelli's minutes, up to 21:08 a night.

Our numbers favor Carolina, 3.55 expected goals to 2.74 tonight. Expected goals measure the quality of chances. At five on five the Hurricanes have taken 58% of them this season, the Islanders 50%. Carolina's power play creates 0.98 expected goals a game against a New York penalty kill that allows 0.90, and the Islanders take 4.6 penalties a game, which keeps handing the other side chances. The goalie matchup is the wrinkle. Projected starter Brandon Bussi is at -4.3 goals saved above expected (how many goals he has stopped beyond what the shots deserved) in six games, while Semyon Varlamov is at +5.7 in four.

Watch Blake, on a seven-game point streak and scoring the lone goal Tuesday; we have him at 60% for a point. Sebastian Aho, a top power-play option, is at 36% to score. For New York, Bo Horvat leads our list at 38% to score. Our under-the-radar pick is Mark Jankowski, who has 4.3 expected goals in his last 10 games from the third line, with 9 high-danger shots. We have him at 25% to score.
